data.name: Benael
data.gender_notes: Benael is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Benael means 'Son of God' or 'God is my sun'. This name holds significant biblical meaning, as it is a derivative of the Hebrew name Ben-Oni, which was given to Jacob's son when he wrestled with the angel and was renamed Ben-Yaacob, meaning 'Son of Jacob'. Benael can also be linked to the Greek name Benjamin, which translates to 'Son of the right hand' or 'Son of the south'. In Christian tradition, Benael represents a strong and devout connection to God, evoking images of courage and faith.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes the sun and God's love and presence
data.etymology: Benael belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God is my sun.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Benael total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Benael holds a rich biblical heritage, making it a meaningful and impactful name in the Christian faith. Its Hebrew origins and associations with the angels and the patriarch Jacob provide a deep and ancient cultural connection to God's word and the stories of the Bible.
data.spiritual_significance: Benael symbolizes a close and personal relationship with God, as 'Son of God' conveys the ultimate connection between humanity and the divine. This name carries a message of faith, strength, and resilience, reminding us of the power of God's love and intervention in our lives. Its link to the name Benjamin, meaning 'Son of the right hand' or 'Son of the south', also resonates with the idea of God's protection and provision, reinforcing the significance of this name as a spiritual reminder of God's presence and faithfulness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Benael: God's grace in strength and light. A name inspired by the biblical figure Ben-Ariel, meaning "son of God's elightenment," symbolizing the divine presence illuminating one's inner and outer world.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Saint Benael, also known as Benen or Benenus, was a 5th-century French hermit and bishop. The name Benael carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Benael is considered one of the early Christian hermits of Gaul, who lived as a recluse and devoted himself to prayer and contemplation. He was later recognized as a bishop and is venerated as a saint.

historical_references.reference: Another Saint Benael, a 7th-century Spanish priest, is believed to have been martyred during the Muslim invasion of the Iberian Peninsula.
historical_references.context: According to legend, Benael was a priest in the town of Cangas de Onis when the Moors invaded. He was captured and tortured, but refused to renounce his faith. He was eventually beheaded and is venerated as a martyr in the Spanish Catholic Church.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Benael' has found modern usage primarily in the realms of Role-playing games (RPGs), fantasy literature and fiction, and tabletop games. In RPGs, Benael is often used as a character name, particularly in games with medieval or fantasy settings. In fantasy literature and fiction, Benael is sometimes used as a protagonist or supporting character in novels or short stories. Finally, in tabletop games, Benael can be found as a character name in various RPG systems, such as Dungeons & Dragons or Pathfinder. The use of the name Benael in these contexts is not limited to those of Christian background and has become a part of the wider fantasy and role-playing communities.
